what_it_does: Maze routing is a chip design step where the toolchain lays out wires between circuit blocks while avoiding obstacles. When accelerated on GPUs for very large chips, the algorithm exhausts GPU memory (the circuit is too big to fit) and wastes time launching many tiny computational kernels. This paper introduces sweep-sharing: allowing multiple independent wires to be routed together in a single pass instead of launching separate jobs for each. It also proposes selective rip-up-and-reroute, which only re-does the wiring for regions that failed, preserving the working portions. Together these cut memory use and runtime substantially on large industrial designs.
